evan_sales: Heads up — Endo Labs POC blocked. POST /v1/generate returns 403 from their CI container. Demo in 3h, can someone please triage?

tara_engineer: Paste the exact curl + response body? 403 usually project binding or scope mismatch.

ev an_sales: They called from CI using the US endpoint: 
```
curl -X POST https://us.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_ENDO' \\
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\
  -d '{"model":"rwx-13b","input":"hello"}'
```
Response: `{"error":{"code":403,"message":"Forbidden: invalid project binding"}}`

sam_support: Two quick checks: 1) decode the token claims to confirm `project` and `scopes`; 2) confirm they are hitting the region endpoint that matches the token (we sometimes include a `region` claim on service tokens). Ask them to run: 
```
printf '%s' "$TOKEN" | cut -d'.' -f2 | base64 -d | jq .
```
Post `project`, `scopes`, and any `region`/`aud` fields.

ev an_sales: Their decoded claims: `{"sub":"svc:endo","project":"endo-poc","scopes":["embeddings:read"],"region":"eu"}`

tara_engineer: Ah — token includes region: "eu" but they're calling the `us` endpoint. Also scope only `embeddings:read`. Model inference requires `inference:invoke`. Two remediation paths: A) have them call `https://eu.api.redwood.ai` (matching token region) OR B) issue a service key bound to the `endo-poc` project with `inference:invoke` and region `us` if they must use the US endpoint.

kyle_ops: I can spin up a short-lived service key bound to endo-poc with the inference scope for the US endpoint. Creating now and will post secure link.

keybot: [bot] service_key_endo_tmp created by kyle_ops for project endo-poc (scopes: ["inference:invoke","embeddings:read"]) — expires: 48h. Ticket: POC-2244.

ev an_sales: I asked the customer to try the new key + X-Project-ID: endo-poc and call the US endpoint. They tried but immediately hit 401; header returned: `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error=\"invalid_token\", error_description=\"signature verification failed\"`.

sam_support: Signature failures often come from copying the key via Windows tools (Notepad adds CRLF) or CI secret injection adding extra quotes/newlines. Ask them to print exact byte length: `echo -n \"$TOKEN\" | wc -c` (or check length in their CI secret UI). Also verify they didn't paste the secure link URL instead of the key.

ev an_sales: Customer said they pasted key from a Windows VM; length was off by 2 bytes. They re-created the secret without CRLF and retried — now 200 OK and streaming works. Demo green.

mia_security: For the customer's security questionnaire: we can rotate keys into their KMS, offer short-lived ephemeral keys, and audit logs are retained 90 days. I posted a short blurb to the shared drive.

kyle_ops: Quick pricing note for Evan to share: hosted trial is fine for demos; recommend Dedicated reserved pools for sustained high-throughput / strict p99 latency. I DM'd a cost ballpark.

tara_engineer: Closing summary: primary root cause = region/endpoint mismatch (token had region=eu, request hit us endpoint) + missing `inference:invoke` scope; secondary friction = key copy introduced CRLF causing signature verification failure. Logged to POC-2244. :white_check_mark:

ev an_sales: Thanks everyone — passing resolution and security snippet to Endo.
